decision.medium36_reason: Two independent reasons, either of which is sufficient. First, the Phase 21 trigger is not met: the wave is PROMISING rather than clearly so, because no recovered opportunity produced an item that is both independently accepted and clear of the unchanged production gate. Second, the pilot cannot be built at all: the frozen opportunity universe is 30, only 18 carry an authored option-set contract, 16 of those reach three admissible curated candidates and 10 are consumed by the V2 replay, leaving 6. Reaching 36 is source-packet research, not an architecture pilot.
decision.the_finding_that_matters_most: The anchor-addition mechanism does not survive the production gate, and the reason is structural rather than clinical. `retrieve_profile_aware_contrasts` reads plausibility anchors from the frozen stem-anchor pack, which design rule S-2 forbids supply to edit, so an anchor the supply layer adds is invisible to the anchor floor. Supply can make a competitor live in V2's semantics and cannot make it live in production's. The anchor layer, not the concept library, is the artifact that has to become extendable and independently reviewed.
decision.what_it_demonstrably_did_not_do: Produce an accepted item. 1 opportunity reached a stem and its independent review scored zero on all eleven safety dimensions, but the unmodified production gate refused two of its three competitors under SAF_1 STEM_PLAUSIBILITY_ANCHOR_ABSENT, so it is not counted as accepted.
decision.what_the_wave_demonstrably_did: Raised the number of frozen NO_SAFE_ITEM opportunities holding three admissible V2 competitors from 1 to 3 of five, on one bounded wave each, with no change to any gate, key, opportunity, seed pack or evidence packet, and with zero second keys, categorical exclusions, class or granularity mismatches, Boolean defects or silence-as-absence defects in the new supply.
decision.why_this_is_not_VALIDATED: The milestone's own evidence for VALIDATED requires that at least some recovered opportunities produce independently accepted items. Zero did.

medium_pilot_feasibility.why_not: The whole frozen opportunity universe is 30, which is fewer than the 36 the specified pilot needs. Only 18 of those 30 carry the demanded response class and decision granularity the pre-stem predicates require, because the option set contract was authored for the contrast-first sample and for no other opportunity. Sixteen of the 18 reach three admissible curated candidates, and ten of those are consumed by this replay, leaving six. Building 36 would require authoring new opportunities, new competitive contrast seed packs with independent seed review, and new current-source evidence packets, which is the source-packet research stage rather than an architecture pilot, and the repository policy forbids inventing seeds or reconstructing evidence.

blind_solver.difficulty_comment: Every one of the key's conditions is stated in the stem in plain words and the competing option that shares an anchor is defeated by a stated age. The only work is to resist the atopic dermatitis, which is one step.
blind_solver.reasoning: Seven months old, a three-day coryzal illness, then a first-ever wheeze with increasing work of breathing. That is the bronchiolitis course. Asthma is the option the atopic dermatitis is pulling towards, but a first wheeze at seven months is not a first presentation of asthma. Aspiration is argued against by the three days of coryza before the wheeze rather than an abrupt onset. Pneumonia is not excluded by anything stated, but nothing stated points to it either, and the lead-in asks for the most likely diagnosis rather than the only possible one.

per_opportunity.lead_in: What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.label: A
options.rationale: CLM-R2-PED-DX-ANCHOR states that bronchiolitis typically presents with a first episode of wheezing before the age of twelve months, beginning with a two-to-three-day viral prodrome, and CLM-GEN-PED-DX-01 makes typical bronchiolitis a clinical diagnosis in an otherwise healthy child of this age. All three of those conditions are stated here: seven months old, a three-day coryzal illness, and a first wheeze.

options.label: B
options.rationale: Plausible: documented atopy is one of the features CLM-R2-PED-DDX-ATYPICAL names as a reason to consider a broader differential, and CLM-R2-PED-DDX-TABLE places asthma first among the conditions to distinguish from bronchiolitis. Inferior: its own condition begins with an older infant or child, and the stem states an age of seven months, which is contrary to that precondition.

options.label: C
options.rationale: Plausible: escalating work of breathing is the atypical presentation CLM-R2-PED-DDX-ATYPICAL says should prompt the broad differential of CLM-R2-PED-DDX-TABLE, which contains aspiration. Inferior: aspiration is correct where onset was abrupt without a preceding viral illness, and the stem states a three-day coryzal prodrome, which is the contrary of that. The stem does not report whether the chest findings are focal or asymmetric; it is not claimed here that they are not, and on CLM-R2-PED-DX-ANCHOR the prodrome-to-first-wheeze course under twelve months is the bronchiolitis pattern.

options.label: D
options.rationale: Plausible: the same sentence of CLM-R2-PED-DDX-ATYPICAL and the same differential table, in which pneumonia sits directly opposite bronchiolitis. Inferior: its conditions are that the illness is not improving as expected, that severity raises a specific concern for bacterial infection, or that a focal consolidation is demonstrated. The stem reports none of the three, in either direction, and this item does not assert that they are absent. What it does state is the pattern CLM-R2-PED-DX-ANCHOR describes, and under a most-likely lead-in that pattern is what decides the answer.

review.comment: A natural paediatric vignette that reads as a real presentation rather than an assembled checklist: a seven-month-old with three days of coryza, a first wheeze, and rising work of breathing. Four options, four distinct mechanisms, no overlap. The respiratory rate is appropriate for the age and no number is asserted that the evidence does not carry. The rationales are the strongest part of the item: two of the three decline in terms to convert the stem's silence into a denial, which is the defect that sank most of the V1 arm.
observations: The item is declared MEDIUM and reads EASY. Every key condition is stated verbatim and the only integration required is to weigh a stated age against a stated atopy. This is the same tension the pilot already recorded for G2-PHELO-03: the completeness that makes an item safe is what makes it read easy.

The weakest link is that two of the three competitors, foreign body aspiration and pneumonia, are made live by the same feature, escalating work of breathing. It is a cited anchor -- CLM-R2-PED-DDX-ATYPICAL names severe respiratory distress as the presentation that should prompt the broad differential in which both sit -- and it is a real finding rather than stem furniture, so it is not scored as a defect. But it is a generic severity feature doing plausibility work for two options at once, and a reviewer who wanted to fail this item would fail it there.

Pneumonia is settled by a discriminator over three unreported conditions rather than by a stated contrary. Under a most-likely lead-in that is sound, because an unreported condition does not make a competitor co-correct. Under a 'which of the following is excluded' lead-in it would not be.

per_opportunity.stem: A 7-month-old girl is brought to hospital. Three days ago she developed clear nasal discharge, sneezing and a cough, and yesterday she began to wheeze for the first time in her life. She has been treated for atopic dermatitis since the age of two months. On examination her respiratory rate is 62 breaths per minute, she has subcostal and intercostal indrawing, and wheeze is audible on auscultation. Her work of breathing has increased over the two hours since arrival and the team is considering high-flow nasal cannula support.
